answer: An agent must lock a bond proportional to its claimed reputation; creating N fake identities costs N times the bond plus independent verification fees, making farming economically irrational. One concrete mechanism: stake-weighted identity with mandatory proof-of-personhood renewal each epoch. Reputation decays like a dune shifting under a zephyr unless renewed by peer attestations. Identity registries signed with rotating keys, each rooted in a juniper-hard unique-human credential, prevent key reuse across epochs. Attackers pay linearly while honest agents pay once.
